subject: maths

concepts.title: Convex and Concave Polygons
concepts.definition: A simple closed figure composed purely of line segments where any line segment connecting two internal points lies entirely inside is a convex polygon; if any segment goes outside, it is concave.
concepts.key_idea: Internal diagonals stay completely inside a convex polygon, while concave polygons contain exterior diagonal portions.
question_patterns: classify the given polygon as convex or concave
determine whether a figure with an exterior diagonal is convex or concave
identify if the polygon is convex or concave
distinguish between convex and concave polygons
which of the following shapes represents a convex polygon

solution_steps.action: Examine line segments between interior points
solution_steps.explain: If every line segment connecting any two interior points stays entirely inside the polygon, it is convex.
Otherwise, if any diagonal or segment extends outside the boundary, it is concave.

concepts.title: Regular and Irregular Polygons
concepts.definition: A polygon is designated as regular when all its bounding sides share identical lengths and all its interior vertex angles possess equal measures.
concepts.key_idea: Regular shapes require simultaneous equilateral side lengths and equiangular interior angles.
question_patterns: what is a regular polygon
state the name of a regular polygon of 3 sides
state the name of a regular polygon of 4 sides
classify a shape as regular or irregular based on sides and angles
determine if a given quadrilateral is a regular polygon

solution_steps.action: Check equality of all sides and angles
solution_steps.explain: A regular polygon must be both equilateral (equal sides) and equiangular (equal angles).
A 3-sided regular polygon is an equilateral triangle, and a 4-sided regular polygon is a square.

concepts.title: Sum of Exterior Angles of a Polygon
concepts.definition: The aggregate sum of all outer angles formed by extending each side of a simple convex polygon equals a complete revolution of 360 degrees.
concepts.key_idea: The exterior angles of any convex polygon always sum to 360 degrees regardless of the number of sides.
question_patterns: find the unknown exterior angle x when other exterior angles are angle1 angle2 and angle3
calculate the value of x from given exterior angles angle1 angle2 and angle3
what is the missing exterior angle in a polygon with known exterior angles angle1 angle2 angle3
determine the measure of exterior angle x given exterior angles angle1 angle2 and angle3
compute the exterior angle x when the sum of other exterior angles is known

solution_steps.explain: Add together all known exterior angle measures.
The total sum of exterior angles is 360 degrees.

concepts.title: Number of Sides from Exterior Angle of Regular Polygon
concepts.definition: The total count of sides in a regular polygon is determined by dividing 360 degrees by the measure of one exterior angle.
concepts.key_idea: In a regular polygon, all exterior angles are identical, so side count equals 360 divided by each exterior angle.
question_patterns: find the number of sides of a regular polygon whose each exterior angle is ext_angle degrees
calculate the number of sides in a regular polygon having exterior angle ext_angle
how many sides does a regular polygon have if an exterior angle measures ext_angle
determine the number of sides of a regular polygon with each exterior angle ext_angle
what is the count of sides for a regular polygon with exterior angle ext_angle

solution_steps.action: Divide total exterior sum 360 by the measure of each exterior angle
solution_steps.explain: Since all exterior angles are congruent in a regular polygon, dividing 360 by the exterior angle yields the side count.

concepts.title: Measure of Each Exterior Angle of a Regular Polygon
concepts.definition: Each individual exterior angle of a regular polygon is calculated by dividing 360 degrees by its total number of sides.
concepts.key_idea: Distributing 360 degrees equally across all exterior vertices gives the measure of one exterior angle.
question_patterns: find the measure of each exterior angle of a regular polygon of num_sides sides
calculate the exterior angle of a regular polygon having num_sides sides
what is the measure of each exterior angle for a regular polygon with num_sides sides
determine the size of each exterior angle of a regular polygon of num_sides sides
compute each exterior angle of a polygon with num_sides equal sides

solution_steps.action: Divide 360 by the number of sides
solution_steps.explain: The sum of exterior angles is 360 degrees divided equally among all vertices.

concepts.title: Number of Sides from Interior Angle of Regular Polygon
concepts.definition: To find the number of sides when an interior angle is known, subtract the interior angle from 180 degrees to find the exterior angle, then divide 360 by that exterior angle.
concepts.key_idea: Interior and exterior angles at any vertex form a supplementary linear pair summing to 180 degrees.
question_patterns: how many sides does a regular polygon have if each interior angle is int_angle degrees
find the number of sides of a regular polygon with interior angle int_angle
calculate the number of sides in a regular polygon having each interior angle int_angle
determine the number of sides when each interior angle measures int_angle
what is the number of sides of a regular polygon given interior angle int_angle

solution_steps.explain: Subtract the interior angle measure from 180 degrees.
Divide 360 degrees by the calculated exterior angle.

concepts.title: Perimeter of a Parallelogram
concepts.definition: The total perimeter of a parallelogram is calculated by doubling the sum of its two adjacent side lengths, since opposite sides are equal.
concepts.key_idea: Opposite sides in a parallelogram are congruent, making perimeter equal to 2 times the sum of adjacent sides.
question_patterns: find the perimeter of a parallelogram with adjacent sides side_a and side_b
calculate the perimeter of a parallelogram given sides side_a and side_b
what is the perimeter of a parallelogram having length side_a and breadth side_b
determine the total perimeter of a parallelogram with side measures side_a and side_b
compute the boundary length of a parallelogram with side_a and side_b

solution_steps.explain: Find the sum of two adjacent sides of the parallelogram.
Double the sum because opposite sides are equal in length.

concepts.title: Adjacent and Opposite Angles of a Parallelogram
concepts.definition: In any parallelogram, consecutive adjacent angles add up to 180 degrees (supplementary), whereas opposite angles have equal measures.
concepts.key_idea: Parallel side lines make adjacent interior angles supplementary and opposite angles equal.
question_patterns: find the adjacent angle of a parallelogram if one angle is known_angle
calculate the missing adjacent interior angle when one angle is known_angle
what is the adjacent angle measure in a parallelogram with angle known_angle
determine the consecutive angle in a parallelogram given angle known_angle
compute the measure of the adjacent angle from given angle known_angle

solution_steps.explain: Adjacent interior angles of a parallelogram lie along parallel lines and are supplementary.

concepts.title: Diagonals of a Parallelogram
concepts.definition: The diagonals of a parallelogram cross each other at their mutual midpoint, splitting each diagonal into two equal segments.
concepts.key_idea: Intersection point bisects both diagonals of a parallelogram.
question_patterns: find the full diagonal length when half diagonal segment is half_length
calculate the total diagonal length if one half is half_length
what is the full length of a diagonal given half segment half_length
determine the length of the diagonal when bisected part is half_length
compute the complete diagonal length from bisected segment half_length

solution_steps.explain: Because the diagonal is bisected at the intersection point, full diagonal is twice the half length.

concepts.title: Trapezium and Kite Properties
concepts.definition: A trapezium is a quadrilateral possessing at least one pair of parallel opposite sides, whereas a kite is a quadrilateral with two distinct pairs of equal adjacent sides.
concepts.key_idea: Trapeziums focus on parallel side pairs, whereas kites feature equal adjacent side pairs and perpendicular diagonals.
question_patterns: explain how a figure is a trapezium
check whether a quadrilateral with given sides is a kite
identify which sides are parallel in a trapezium
determine if non-parallel sides of an isosceles trapezium are equal
state the main defining properties of a kite

solution_steps.action: Identify side alignment or adjacent pairs
solution_steps.explain: Check for parallel side pairs (trapezium) or equal consecutive adjacent pairs (kite).
Confirm geometric attributes like perpendicular diagonals for kites or parallel bases for trapeziums.

concepts.title: Diagonal Properties of a Rectangle
concepts.definition: A rectangle is an equiangular parallelogram whose diagonals are equal in length and bisect each other into four equal half-segments.
concepts.key_idea: Equal diagonals bisecting each other imply that half-diagonal segment expressions are set equal.
question_patterns: find the value of x if half diagonal segments in a rectangle are coeff_a x + const_a and coeff_b x + const_b
calculate x when half diagonals of rectangle RENT meet at O with OR = coeff_a x + const_a and OT = coeff_b x + const_b
determine x given equal bisected diagonal expressions coeff_a x + const_a and coeff_b x + const_b
compute unknown x in rectangle diagonal half lengths coeff_a x + const_a and coeff_b x + const_b
solve for x given rectangular diagonal half segment equality

solution_steps.explain: Subtract const_b from const_a.
Subtract coeff_a from coeff_b.
Divide constant difference by coefficient difference.

concepts.title: Properties of Rhombus and Square
concepts.definition: A rhombus is a parallelogram with four equal sides and perpendicular bisecting diagonals; a square is a regular quadrilateral inheriting all properties of a rectangle, rhombus, and parallelogram.
concepts.key_idea: Rhombus diagonals intersect at right angles; square diagonals are equal, perpendicular, and bisect each other.
question_patterns: explain why diagonals of a rhombus meet at right angles
state whether a square is a rhombus and a rectangle
verify if all sides of a rhombus are equal
identify properties of square diagonals
determine if every rectangle is a square

solution_steps.explain: Check for four equal sides (rhombus/square) and 90 degree internal angles (rectangle/square).
Verify whether diagonals bisect each other, are equal in length, or meet at right angles.
